decision.summaryForCoordinator: The most interesting result is that the dispatch's own equality attack could not have caught the likeliest citation error on this gate. Two catalogs exist at 0444 — g20-named-corpus-catalog.v1 and .v2 — with identical namedCorpusNotAuthored, registerRow and namedGate, so 'named initial states equal live G20 v1' passes against either. I diffed them: v2 adds findingDisposition and states it lands CLAUDE-G20CAT-V1-SF1 by carrying live slashJoiner and surfacesInOrder. The subject cites v2, and sdk-leftover-join.v4 independently treats v2 as the live catalog. Any later conformance check on this family should test the cited version, not only the list. Two prohibitions needed reading rather than counting. 'API' occurs eight times, every one inside a negation or inside the obligation id OBL-SDK-API-RESERVED, and no method, signature, type, namespace, framework or binding is named — with the bare-integer set at 1 and 26, no version or constant exists either; the live DR-125 row independently records 'exact APIs/frameworks deferred'. SARIF occurs three times, all inside the quoted live class name that also appears verbatim in the live DR-G20 register cell, so nothing is advertised. I also traced the one sentence attributing a record to a leftoverNameNote without naming whose: sdk-leftover-join.v4 carries that exact sentence in its own role AND holds OBL-DR125-ACTIVATION at rides-DR-118, while live G20 v1's leftoverNameNote states the fact directly — true at both levels. Cardinality holds: G20 v1's namedCorpusNote says the eight slash-joined surfaces are cells of one class and names four things not to invent as extra ids, and the subject keeps the eight inside one quoted string, creates exactly one initialState, and contains zero occurrences of T-1, NT-4 or NT-7. The separator is U+00D7 rather than ASCII, byte-identical across live, subject and catalog. Both cited joins were re-measured at source and every limb of both role claims is true, all nine digests match, and the subject carries no file08StatusToken — correct for an input corpus and removing the import-a-token failure mode. Twenty-three attacks run, twenty-three refuted, zero findings. One family-wide note: like the g18 input corpus, this artifact calls itself 'This catalog' three times despite being an input corpus, and in the namedCatalog role the referent is ambiguous — both readings are true and the operative fields all say 'This artifact', so it is naming hygiene a successor could tidy across the class in one pass. Disclosure: all four cited claude2 reviews are my own, including two joins from earlier in this session; every standing reported here was re-derived from live bytes rather than from those verdicts.
